title: Thirty-Three In The Queue
mood: too old for it and glad to be there
subject: queueing for a club where everyone else is twenty
caption: UK garage in the two-step style. Shuffled two-step drum pattern with skipped kicks and swung sixteenth hi-hats, short organ chord stabs on the offbeats, a wobbling sub bass, pitched-up and chopped R&B vocal samples answering the lead, a filtered string pad on the chorus. Swung and skippy with a heavy sub and a crisp bright top, mixed for a club system. Male voice, conversational in the verses with a light melodic lift on the hook, no autotune. 132 BPM, F minor. Too old for it and glad to be there. No four-on-the-floor house kick, no trap hi-hat rolls, no rap verse, no acoustic instruments, no key change.
lyrics:
[Intro - two-step drums and organ stab]

[Verse 1]
Queue goes round the corner and everybody's twenty
I'm thirty-three in a jacket I bought for a wedding
Bouncer looks at my ID longer than he looks at theirs
Then he laughs, and he lets me in, and he says "big man"

[Pre-Chorus]
I came here for one song
I don't even know if they still play it

[Chorus]
Thirty-three in the queue
And the bass still finds my ribs the same way it used to
Nobody in here knows what I do on a Monday
For two hours I'm not anybody's anything

[Verse 2]
Girl next to me asks if I'm somebody's dad
I say no, I'm somebody's ex and somebody's tenant
She laughs and hands me her water without asking
That's the most looked-after I have felt all year

[Chorus]
Thirty-three in the queue
And the bass still finds my ribs the same way it used to
Nobody in here knows what I do on a Monday
For two hours I'm not anybody's anything, and they played it

[Outro - vocal chop and sub]
Taxi? No. I'm walking.
Forty minutes. I'll feel it Tuesday.
